title: Algiers oak-tree picnics and the Big Dorsey story
summary: He describes Sunday picnics under oak trees with brass bands, and interviewers ask about a Dorsey story from Fess.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Under the oak trees, yeah. White picnics and colored picnics, they had on the oak trees, big oak trees. They used to have on the Sunday night, Sunday night, you know, they'd have big picnics there. Or they'd have big time there, the brass bands sometimes they played. You see, and I'll open the night, they'd have the brass bands. Now I'm in there, Dorsey, big father. He had a big, nice band in there. Peter, his father was playing guitar. Peter, yeah, his father was playing with Dorsey's band. And he used to have a band come at Sox's Lane and Louie Arts. Had a big flat foam on a Sunday. They'd come there and start up at four o'clock. Three until twelve.
Peter, was that the Dorsey that Fess told us about one time when they didn't give him anything to eat? They asked him something about cheese? Big Dorsey, yeah.
He used to play these, yeah. Big Dorsey. What was that story? Eh?
What was that story? Oh yeah, that's when Fess pulled that with another problem.

Yeah, one time Fess mentioned that to Dandy Lewis, was it, or somebody, and he was going to hit him. And he thought they were laughing at him, but they were laughing about this fellow Dorsey. Dorsey, yeah. One time they didn't give the band anything to eat a drink.
Dorsey. Do you remember hearing about that?
Was that any, did all the musicians know about that?
What was that? Well Fess was telling me, but I didn't understand that. No. I didn't know what that was.
I think that was something like the fellow that went for the fish and something like that. Something like that.
